components.name: BlurPass
components.reason: src/webgpu/Materials/BlurPass is still the WebGL implementation — its own first line says 'TODO: Convert GLSL shaders to TSL for WebGPU'. It imports the legacy GLSL ConvolutionMaterial plus WebGLRenderer, which three/webgpu does not export, so it is deliberately excluded from the /webgpu barrel. A TSL ConvolutionMaterial already exists next to it, which is why this is agent-ok rather than human-only. Tracked in #2811.

components.name: Effects
components.reason: Wraps three-stdlib's EffectComposer, which is WebGL-only. WebGPU postprocessing goes through three's own RenderPipeline (useRenderPipeline in r3f v10), which is a different architecture rather than a port of this one.

components.name: MeshDiscardMaterial
components.reason: The heuristic flags this human-only because the legacy file uses ShaderMaterial, but that is exactly what gets replaced. webgpu/DiscardMaterial already exists; this is a NodeMaterial with discard() in TSL plus the same thin JSX wrapper. Mechanical.

components.name: shaderMaterial
components.reason: A factory for GLSL ShaderMaterials. TSL's equivalent is node-graph construction, a fundamentally different authoring model — WebGPU users write TSL directly rather than calling a GLSL factory.

components.name: ShadowAlpha
components.reason: Patches the depth material's GLSL through onBeforeCompile to carry alpha into shadows. Same constraint as useBoxProjectedEnv — needs a new TSL implementation rather than a port.

components.name: Text

components.name: useBoxProjectedEnv
components.reason: Implemented by patching a built-in material's GLSL through onBeforeCompile. TSL has no onBeforeCompile equivalent; box-projected environment mapping on WebGPU would be a new node-based implementation, not a port.
